summary: Tonga admits EU, EEA, Swiss and Israeli passport holders without a visa for 90 days within 180, and issues a free visitor's visa on arrival for 30 days — extendable to six months — to citizens of the US, UK, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea and most Commonwealth and Pacific countries; other nationalities must obtain a visa before traveling.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. There is no yellow fever or malaria risk in Tonga itself.

source.name: Tonga Ministry of Revenue and Customs — Immigration Division

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not a condition of entry, but Vaiola Hospital in Nuku'alofa handles only basic cases and anything serious means an air ambulance to New Zealand — travel insurance including medical evacuation is strongly recommended.

source.name: Tonga Ministry of Revenue and Customs — Immigration Division

onwardTicket.text: A confirmed onward or return ticket is required for the visitor's visa and is checked by airlines at check-in.

source.name: Tonga Ministry of Revenue and Customs — Immigration Division

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors must show sufficient funds for their stay and confirmed accommodation. No fixed amount is published. A booking confirmation and a card or recent bank statement is normally enough.

source.name: Tonga Ministry of Revenue and Customs — Immigration Division

declarations.name: Passenger arrival and customs declaration card
declarations.text: Complete the combined immigration and customs arrival card handed out before landing at Fua'amotu airport; declare all food, plant and animal products on it.

source.name: Tonga Ministry of Revenue and Customs — Immigration Division

currencyLimits.text: Cash above the reporting threshold set under Tonga's anti-money-laundering rules must be declared on arrival and departure. Check the current amount with Tonga Customs before traveling with large sums.

source.name: Tonga Ministry of Revenue and Customs — Immigration Division

notes: Quarantine rules are strict: fresh fruit, vegetables, meat, seeds, plants and unprocessed wooden items must be declared and are often confiscated.
Firearms, ammunition and offensive weapons require prior police authorization; drugs offenses carry severe penalties.
Taking whale products, turtle shell, coral or protected shells out of Tonga is prohibited.

payments.text: Resorts, larger hotels and some restaurants in Nuku'alofa and Neiafu take cards, often with a surcharge. ATMs are limited to Tongatapu, Vava'u and Ha'apai, so carry paʻanga in cash for markets, taxis, boats and outer islands.

safety.text: Tonga is a calm, community-minded country with little violent crime; opportunistic theft and occasional late-night trouble around bars in Nuku'alofa are the main risks. Natural hazards matter more — cyclones from November to April, and an active volcanic and seismic zone.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Tonga travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to October is dry, cooler and outside the cyclone season; humpback whales are in Tongan waters roughly July to October, which is the peak reason most visitors come.

tips.text: Sunday is constitutionally protected as a day of rest: shops, restaurants, flights and most tours stop, and commerce is prohibited. Buy food on Saturday, and expect only resorts and church services to be open.
Tonga is conservative and Christian — cover shoulders and knees away from resorts, keep swimwear to the beach and pool, and dress up for church, where visitors are genuinely welcome.
Swimming with humpback whales is allowed only with a licensed operator and a set number of swimmers in the water. Book a licensed Vava'u or Ha'apai operator well ahead for the July–October season.
The cyclone season runs November to April, and Tonga also sits on an active volcanic arc. Check advisories before traveling in those months and make sure your insurance covers disruption.
There are no ATMs on most outer islands and boat schedules change with the weather. Carry enough paʻanga in small notes and leave a buffer day before your international flight.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tonga?
faq.answer: Most visitors do not need one in advance. EU, EEA, Swiss and Israeli passport holders enter without a visa for up to 90 days in 180. Citizens of the US, UK, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Singapore and most Commonwealth and Pacific countries receive a free visitor's visa on arrival for 31 days. Other nationalities must apply to Tonga Immigration before traveling.

faq.question: How long is the visa on arrival valid for?
faq.answer: 31 days. It is issued free at Fua'amotu airport on presentation of a passport valid 6 months beyond departure, an onward ticket and proof of funds, and can be extended month by month at the Immigration Division up to a total stay of six months.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Tonga?
faq.answer: Yes. Apply at the Immigration Division in Nuku'alofa before your current visa expires, taking your passport, onward ticket and proof of funds. Extensions are granted in monthly steps to a maximum total stay of about six months.

faq.question: Is everything really closed on Sunday in Tonga?
faq.answer: Almost. Sunday trading is restricted by the constitution, so shops, most restaurants, tours and domestic flights do not operate. Resorts feed their guests and church services are a highlight, but plan arrivals, departures and shopping around it.

faq.question: Can I pay by card in Tonga?
faq.answer: Only in resorts, larger hotels and some Nuku'alofa and Neiafu businesses, usually with a surcharge. ATMs exist on Tongatapu, Vava'u and Ha'apai but not on smaller islands, so bring Tongan paʻanga in cash for day-to-day spending.
